findings.text: admitting_partition duplicates partition_for_bound (:973) and the two can disagree: a configured partition_max_seconds below 3600 (say all_debug 1800) lets a declared 2400 be accepted, while partition_for_bound submits it to all_debug with --time=00:40:00, over that partition's maximum, so the arm is ended mid-run despite the declaration check passing.
partition_max_seconds reads a configured limit that parse_gate_duration cannot parse as unbounded, so a typo in landing.partition_max_seconds silently removes the ceiling instead of being refused.

the head gate log's revision line names 398a0d09, the base sha, because the arm ran against the worktree before its commit; a reader comparing it to the promoted head cannot tell the head arm measured the change, though my re-run at c0e484cb gives 4 passed.

item_verdicts.diff: read the single commit 398a0d09..c0e484cb commit by commit; it changes reckon/crew/landing_measure.py (+121/-5), reckon/crew/promotion_records.py (+23/-2), reckon/crew/queue_landing.py (+16/-0), reckon/crew_run_commands.py (+66/-3) and adds 218 test lines, all inside scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: tests/test_a_declared_gate_duration_bounds_its_arms.py:150-171 asserts both arms carry --time at least 4500 on a partition whose table maximum admits it, :173-190 keeps an undeclared run at the project's 600s floor, and :191-210 refuses a 20000s declaration naming 04:00:00 and long_pool; the manifest records 4 passed at head, and I reproduced 4 passed at c0e484cb in a scratch extraction.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is to let a run declare how long its gate takes and floor its landing arms by it; reckon/crew_run_commands.py:4625 adds crew declare-gate --duration and reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:1342 raises measure_run's timeout floor with it.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the literal gate command, both gate logs, measurement_module=/tmp/mcintos-s54-qgG31V/base/reckon/crew/landing_measure.py, measurement_cwd, the negative control and status complete.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the node's declared list; the single commit touches five paths and every one is among them.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_declared_gate_duration_bounds_its_arms.py:167 asserts each submitted --time is at least the declared 4500, and the base arm reddens it with 'assert 600.0 >= 4500.0' on --time=00:10:00, so reinstating the regression fails the guard.
justifications.evidence: the head arm's first line at /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20261123T112715625088-delivered-work-lands-without-a-coordinator-s54/s54-head-gate.log:1 records revision 398a0d09 (the base) although it ran from the worktree, so the receipt names a revision it did not run at; added failures are 0, derived from 10 base ids and 4 head ids with all 4 head ids present at base.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:710-800 follows the module's regex-plus-helper idiom with mechanism comments and no plan or ticket labels.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:1342 and :1621 floor every arm's timeout with declared_duration, and reckon/crew/queue_landing.py:1203 reads the declaration from the run's own pointer so only that run moves.
justifications.reuse: admitting_partition at reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:779 re-implements the partition-selection capability partition_for_bound owns at :973 without extending it, so it scores at the rubric ceiling.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path (reckon/crew/landing_measure.py, reckon/crew/promotion_records.py, reckon/crew/queue_landing.py, reckon/crew_run_commands.py, tests/test_a_declared_gate_duration_bounds_its_arms.py) lies inside the declared write paths.
